text:
sam: Quick pre-review notes for today's compact-density sweep on the compare table. Main problem: when rows collapse we lose both the perf badges and the pin affordance. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/compact-density/compare-sweep :mag:

hana: Saw the prototype. My read: small screens and dense rows make the current inline pin practically invisible. Users also told us in research they expect a persistent presence once they pin something.

prateek: Two approaches we explored in the lab: (A) visual gutter pin that persists across collapse, minimal width impact; (B) compact indicator chip attached to the model name when collapsed ("Pinned • v2"). Chip is clearer but can overflow in DE/FR locales.

lucy: Accessibility notes: the performance badge color pair we use (mint on white) fails contrast at 12px per Axe. We should either use a darker token or add a 1px stroke + text fallback on hover. Also the pin icon currently doesn't expose aria-pressed or aria-label.

sam: UX decision proposals: 1) Default to gutter pin (small, always-visible). 2) For users with "dense view" turned on, show a single compact pinned strip that appears above the table when >1 pinned. 3) Add a user preference: "Keep pinned rows visible when filtering". Thoughts?

hana: I like 1 + 2 hybrid. For the strip, keep it collapsible and dismissible. It should only appear if pinned models would otherwise be off-screen after filter changes.

prateek: Frontend constraints: gutter pin requires a pseudo-layer to avoid shifting table column widths. Implementation idea: absolutely-position a hit-target in the row container and keep it outside normal cell flow. That avoids layout thrash.

lucy: Microcopy: change tooltip from "Pin version" to "Pin for side-by-side compare". For screen readers, use aria-label="Toggle pin for compare" and aria-pressed true/false. Example:

```
<button class=\"cmp-pin\" aria-pressed=\"false\" aria-label=\"Toggle pin for compare\">📌</button>
```

prateek: Interaction edge-cases: 1) If user pins then applies a filter that excludes it, we should surface a non-blocking toast: "Pinned model hidden by filters. Show pinned models? [Show]". 2) Keyboard shortcut: while a row is focused, pressing "p" toggles pin. Ensure focus doesn't jump.

sam: Analytics: track events pin.toggled {pinned: true|false, location: sidebar|gutter|strip, via: keyboard|click}. We'll need this to measure discoverability across variants.

hana: A11y detail: performance badges should include role=\"img\" and aria-label like "Latency 23ms, Cost $0.002 per 1k tokens". Tooltips should be reachable via keyboard and not rely purely on hover.

lucy: Also, for colorblind users the badges should not be solely color-coded. Add a small icon or initials (L=low latency, M=med, H=high) that appears on narrow widths or in dense mode.

prateek: Dev note: the sticky strip for >1 pins should be virtualized when table is large to avoid rendering overhead. We'll prototype with the overlay component we already have.

sam: Can we try two quick prototypes in the review: (A) gutter pin + chip fallback for collapsed rows (B) gutter pin + compact sticky strip for multi-pin. We'll A/B internally on the prototype to get quick feedback.

hana: For the prototypes include keyboard flows, aria attributes, and contrast-adjusted badge tokens. Also include copy variations for the toast and tooltips.

design-bot: Created ticket UX-6082: "Compare: compact density pin visibility + badges contrast + keyboard" and attached frames for prototypes A/B.

product-ops: Added acceptance criteria: - pin is keyboard focusable and toggled by Space/Enter and 'p' shortcut - pinned rows optionally stay visible when filters applied - performance badges meet 4.5:1 contrast or have text/icon fallback - analytics events emitted for pin interactions. Assigned to eng-frontend and ux-research.

sam: Great. I'll demo both prototypes and we'll capture quick metrics during the review. If folks can review the copy variations before 10:30 that would help. Thanks! :thumbsup:
